recognize_zh: 新生兒周邊血中可見許多小而深染、缺乏中央淡染區的球形紅血球（microspherocytes），合併偏藍的多染性紅血球與一個有核紅血球，符合 ABO 不相容所致的新生兒溶血病。
features: Numerous microspherocytes: small, dense red cells lacking central pallor
Polychromatophilic larger bluish red cells indicating reticulocytosis
Nucleated red blood cell (upper center) with dense, lobulated nucleus
Two segmented neutrophils and scattered platelets
Mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional irregular or crenated forms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous microspherocytes lacking central pallor, admixed with polychromatophilic red cells and a circulating nucleated red blood cell. Two segmented neutrophils and adequate platelets are present. No schistocytes or intraerythrocytic parasites are seen. In a neonate, findings are consistent with immune hemolysis, and the prominent spherocytes are typical of hemolytic disease of the newborn due to ABO incompatibility; confirmation with maternal and infant blood typing and DAT is recommended.

ddx.vs: Hereditary spherocytosis has a negative DAT, a positive family history, and abnormal EMA binding, whereas ABO HDN is DAT-positive with mother-infant ABO mismatch.

ddx.dx: Rh hemolytic disease of the newborn
ddx.vs: Rh disease usually shows fewer spherocytes but more nucleated red cells and more severe anemia, with a strongly positive DAT and anti-D.
Normal neonatal blood contains macrocytes and occasional nRBCs but not numerous microspherocytes.
